items.text: What if the Earth suddenly stopped spinning? The planet stops. You don't.
At the equator, the ground races east at one thousand six hundred seventy kilometers per hour. If the Earth hits the brakes, everything not bolted to bedrock keeps flying.
The atmosphere doesn't stop either: winds faster than any hurricane wipe out cities and forests in minutes.
The oceans do the same. Giant tsunamis smash into the coasts and surge hundreds of kilometers inland.
Then the Earth changes shape. Without rotation, the bulge at the equator disappears: the oceans drain toward the poles, and one single, colossal supercontinent rises along the equator.
And one day lasts an entire year: six months of scorching light, six months of freezing night.
Life could only survive on the border between day and night, in a sunset that never ends.
Luckily, Earth's spin slows by just two milliseconds per century. The world will keep turning.
